messages:
rachel: Trying the quickstart from my laptop but going through our company bastion (ssh -R) — first call just times out and curl shows: 'curl: (35) error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure'
june: Uh interesting — are you tunneling a hostname or an IP? reverse tunnels usually break SNI so certs don't match
rachel: I did 'ssh -R 8443:localhost:8443 bastion' and then curl https://localhost:8443/v1/health — expected a JSON, got the TLS error. The quickstart uses the redwood client which hits api.play.redwood.ai originally, I tried rewriting host header to the tunnel
sam: If your tunnel is localhost:8443 but the cert is for api.redwood.ai you'll get subject name mismatch. Two quick ways: 1) use --resolve in curl to map api.play.redwood.ai to 127.0.0.1:8443 2) set REDWOOD_API_URL to http://localhost:8443 for local dev
rachel: tried --resolve but then the client fails later with 'session creation blocked: workspace billing required' which is weird — this is a fresh org I created this morning
cheng: That part sounds like billing gating — if an org hasn't accepted the trial billing flow some endpoints will return a 402/blocked policy. But weird that it shows behind your tunnel as a TLS error earlier
june: Likely two overlapping issues: 1) TLS/SNI mismatch causing the handshake error, and 2) server-side policy returning a blocked response once TLS is bypassed. They're surfacing differently depending on how you proxy.
rachel: repro steps I ran: 
```
ssh -R 8443:localhost:8443 bastion
export REDWOOD_API_URL=https://api.play.redwood.ai
curl -v --resolve api.play.redwood.ai:8443:127.0.0.1 https://api.play.redwood.ai:8443/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
```
curl then shows a JSON with {"error":"billing_required","message":"workspace needs billing setup"} when I pass the host resolve.
sam: OK so the platform is doing the right thing for the billing gate. For the TLS part, we should doc the tunnel pattern: use --resolve or set REDWOOD_API_URL to http://localhost:8443 and disable TLS in the dev token path. We don't recommend reverse-tunneling the production hostname because certs won't match.
cheng: I'll add a short blurb to the quickstart about tunnel caveats and a troubleshooting note for "billing_required" errors pointing at the org billing UI. Also adding an example curl --resolve snippet.
rachel: thanks. small ask — can the error surface be clearer in the client? 'workspace needs billing setup' is fine but earlier it surfaced as a TLS handshake and was confusing
june: Agreed. We should prefer a visible JSON error and a 402 code rather than letting proxies mask it. I'll file a follow-up issue to check how our ingress and reverse proxy behave with SNI mismatch and whether we can detect and return a clearer message when the client host header maps to a different host.
devex-bot: new issue created: DEVEX-1129 "quickstart: tunnel TLS mismatch + billing gating confusing errors" — assigned to june
rachel: awesome. For now the workaround for anyone doing local dev behind bastion: set REDWOOD_API_URL to http://127.0.0.1:8443 and use an API key from a workspace with billing enabled or accept trial on the org console. :+1:
sam: added a short PR to the quickstart README with that workaround and the --resolve example. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart/pull/58
cheng: closing the thread once PR lands. thanks for the clear repro!"
